Experimental Phase 3 R methods: advanced contrast

etr-advanced-contrast.Rd

Native R scientific methods and diagnostics under active qualification; these functions are not cleared for a CRAN release or calibrated inference.

Usage

etr_bootstrap_group_contrast(
  x,
  participant,
  group,
  B = 399L,
  alpha = 0.05,
  seed = 3L
)

etr_multilevel_reconstruct(
  fit,
  n_between = NULL,
  n_within = NULL
)

etr_multilevel_diagnostics(
  fit
)

Arguments

x

A native trajectory object, sparse collection, numeric sequence, or validated diagnostic according to the function.

participant

Participant identifiers by curve, or a metadata-column name.

group

Exactly two group labels, each constant within participant.

B

Number of participant-level bootstrap draws, at least 39.

alpha

Target nominal miscoverage in (0,1); calibration not guaranteed.

seed

Deterministic random seed.

fit

A fitted native R model result of the expected class.

n_between

Number of between-participant components.

n_within

Number of within-participant components.

Details

These methods have explicitly limited scientific scope. Sparse estimation uses fdapace when requested; functional mixed models use optional refund. Marginal sparse fits do not estimate joint cross-channel covariance. Cluster bootstrap resamples participants, not trials. Transfer entropy describes discrete predictive information, not causality, and its diagnostic p-values are not generally calibrated. See docs/phase3-expansion-methods.md for independent simulation contracts.

Value

A typed native model, diagnostic, Monte Carlo audit, or base R plot; returned components are documented in the Phase 3 methods article.
